    How to use
    
  
      
    
    1. On the Convert tab, choose or drop your disc files. Pick the .cue (or .gdi) together with all of its .bin/track files.
      2. 
    
    2. Each game appears as a card. The right chdman command is chosen automatically; open Options to change compression, hunk size or the output name.
      3. 
    
    3. Press Create CHD on a card, or Start all at the bottom. Jobs run one after another.
      4. 
    
    4. When a job finishes, press Download (on iPhone and iPad the button is called Save to Files and opens the share sheet, which also works inside apps that cannot download). On desktop Chrome/Edge you can Save all to folder.
      5. 
  
    
  
    Add .chd files to extract them back to .cue/.bin, .gdi, .iso or a raw image, to verify their checksums, or to see their details.
    

    


    
  
    Which conversion should I use?
    
  
    
  
    
    
    SystemYour filesUse

    Dreamcast.gdi + tracks, or Redump .cue + .binCD (GD-ROM is detected)
    
      
    PlayStation 2DVD games: .iso · CD games: .cue + .binDVD · CD
    
      
    PSP.isoDVD, hunk size 2,048
    
      
    Arcade and computer hard disks.img, .hdd (raw)Hard disk
    
      
    LaserDisc arcade games.aviLaserDisc
    
        
  
    
  
    
  
    A lone .bin without its .cue still works for single-track data discs (a cue is generated), but for discs with music tracks always add the original .cue.
    

    


    
  
    Game identification and renaming
    
  
    Every disc you add is examined to find its console (PlayStation 1/2/PSP, Saturn, Sega CD, Dreamcast, PC Engine CD, PC-FX, Neo Geo CD, 3DO, CD-i, Amiga CD32/CDTV, NAOMI and more) and its serial number, read from the disc's own boot files and headers.
    
  
    The game is then looked up in a built-in copy of the Redump database (about 42,000 discs, via libretro-database, version 2026.08.01). When a track's size and CRC-32 checksum match, the dump is an exact, verified copy; otherwise the serial number is used. Results are named after the official title, for example Metal Gear Solid (USA) (Disc 1) (Rev 1).chd. You can turn this off in Settings or type your own name in Options.
    
  
    For existing .chd files, choose Rename to save a copy with the official name.
    

    


    
  
    Good to know
    
  
    Privacy
    
  
    Nothing is uploaded. The real chdman from MAME runs inside your browser as WebAssembly; files are read directly from your device.
    
  
    Big files
    
  
    Results are written to the browser's private storage on disk (not to memory), so multi-gigabyte DVD images work if your device has the free space. Download results when they are ready; the storage is cleared when you use Free temporary storage or reopen the page. On desktop Chrome and Edge you can instead have results written straight into a folder of your choice (Settings → Where to keep results).
    
  
    Speed
    
  
    Creating a CHD is CPU-heavy. This page spreads compression over several CPU threads (see Settings). Expect a few minutes for a CD on a computer and longer on a phone. Faster to create in Options trades a little size for a lot of speed.
    
  
    On phones and tablets
    
  
    The layout adapts to your screen, text size, notch, rotation and keyboard. In a normal browser the whole page scrolls; inside apps that preview files (and when installed on the home screen) the header stays fixed and only the content scrolls. If scrolling ever feels wrong, change it in Settings → Scrolling; Settings → Screen info shows what your device reports. 
    
  
    Keep this page open and in the foreground while it works; the screen is kept awake automatically. If the browser suspends the tab, the job may stop and need to be restarted.
    
  
    Compatibility of the results
    
  
    The CHDs are standard CHD v5 files made by chdman from the official MAME 0.289 release, with the same checksums as desktop chdman 0.289 (for data, the very same bytes as the official build), so they work in MAME, RetroArch, DuckStation, PCSX2, PPSSPP, Flycast and other emulators. The Zstandard option needs a recent emulator build.
    
  
    Everything else
    
  
    The Advanced tab exposes every chdman command and option: copy, createraw, parent CHDs, hard disk templates, addmeta, delmeta, dumpmeta, listtemplates and more.
    

    


    
  
    About and licenses
    
  
    Discpress contains chdman from MAME 0.289 (the official release, tag mame0289), compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten. Two small browser-specific changes were made: a file-system bridge for reading your files and writing results, and multi-threaded compression through helper workers. The full list of source changes is below.

+#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
+void chd_file_compressor::wasm_par_complete_item(void *itemp, uint32_t crc16, const uint8_t *sha1, int compression, uint32_t complen, const uint8_t *data)
+{
+	work_item &item = *reinterpret_cast<work_item *>(itemp);
+	item.m_hash[0].m_crc16 = util::crc16_t(uint16_t(crc16));
+	memcpy(item.m_hash[0].m_sha1.m_raw, sha1, sizeof(item.m_hash[0].m_sha1.m_raw));
+	item.m_compression = int8_t(compression);
+	item.m_complen = complen;
+	memcpy(item.m_compressed, data, complen);
+	item.m_status = WS_COMPLETE;
+}
+
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE void wasm_par_complete(void *item, uint32_t crc16, const uint8_t *sha1, int compression, uint32_t complen, const uint8_t *data)
+{
+	chd_file_compressor::wasm_par_complete_item(item, crc16, sha1, compression, complen, data);
+}
+#endif

+++ wasm_helper.cpp (new file)
+// Browser build helper: lets a secondary WebAssembly instance (running in a
+// helper Web Worker) compress CHD hunks exactly the way chd_file_compressor
+// would, so the main chdman instance can spread compression over many cores.
+#include "chd.h"
+#include "chdcodec.h"
+#include "hashing.h"
+#include "ioprocsvec.h"
+
+#include <emscripten.h>
+
+#include <cstring>
+#include <memory>
+#include <unordered_set>
+#include <vector>
+
+namespace {
+std::vector<uint8_t> s_store;
+std::unique_ptr<chd_file> s_chd;
+std::unique_ptr<chd_compressor_group> s_group;
+std::vector<uint8_t> s_in, s_out;
+uint32_t s_hunkbytes = 0;
+std::unordered_set<uint64_t> s_seen; // hashes of hunks this helper already compressed
+}
+
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE int wasm_helper_init(uint32_t hunkbytes, uint32_t unitbytes, uint32_t c0, uint32_t c1, uint32_t c2, uint32_t c3)
+{
+	try
+	{
+		chd_codec_type comp[4] = { c0, c1, c2, c3 };
+		s_group.reset();
+		s_chd.reset();
+		s_store.clear();
+		s_chd = std::make_unique<chd_file>();
+		util::random_read_write::ptr file = std::make_unique<util::vector_read_write_adapter<uint8_t>>(s_store);
+		std::error_condition err = s_chd->create(std::move(file), uint64_t(hunkbytes), hunkbytes, unitbytes, comp);
+		if (err)
+			return -1;
+		s_group = std::make_unique<chd_compressor_group>(*s_chd, comp);
+		s_hunkbytes = hunkbytes;
+		s_seen.clear();
+		s_in.assign(hunkbytes, 0);
+		s_out.assign(hunkbytes, 0);
+		return 0;
+	}
+	catch (...)
+	{
+		return -2;
+	}
+}
+
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE uint8_t *wasm_helper_inbuf() { return s_in.data(); }
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE uint8_t *wasm_helper_outbuf() { return s_out.data(); }
+
+// result[0] = compressed length, result[1] = crc16; sha1out receives 20 bytes.
+// returns the codec index (-1 = stored uncompressed)
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE int wasm_helper_compress(uint32_t *result, uint8_t *sha1out)
+{
+	result[1] = uint16_t(util::crc16_creator::simple(s_in.data(), s_hunkbytes));
+	util::sha1_t const sha1 = util::sha1_creator::simple(s_in.data(), s_hunkbytes);
+	std::memcpy(sha1out, sha1.m_raw, sizeof(sha1.m_raw));
+
+	// a repeat of a hunk this helper already handled (earlier in the file) will be
+	// stored as a "copy from self" by the writer, so don't waste time compressing it;
+	// returns -2 and the writer compresses it itself if it turns out not to be a copy
+	uint64_t key;
+	std::memcpy(&key, sha1.m_raw, sizeof(key));
+	key ^= uint64_t(result[1]) << 48;
+	if (!s_seen.insert(key).second)
+	{
+		result[0] = 0;
+		return -2;
+	}
+	if (s_seen.size() > 262144)
+		s_seen.clear();
+
+	uint32_t complen = s_hunkbytes;
+	int8_t const compression = s_group->find_best_compressor(s_in.data(), s_out.data(), complen);
+	result[0] = complen;
+	return compression;
+}
+
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Probe API: read sectors from an existing CHD so the page can identify the
+// game (system, serial, title) without extracting it.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#include "cdrom.h"
+
+namespace {
+std::unique_ptr<chd_file> p_chd;
+std::unique_ptr<cdrom_file> p_cd;
+}
+
+// returns 1 = CD/GD-ROM, 2 = other (DVD, HD, raw), -1 = cannot open, -2 = needs parent
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE int wasm_probe_open(const char *path)
+{
+	p_cd.reset();
+	p_chd.reset();
+	try
+	{
+		p_chd = std::make_unique<chd_file>();
+		std::error_condition err = p_chd->open(path);
+		if (err == chd_file::error::REQUIRES_PARENT)
+			return -2;
+		if (err)
+			return -1;
+		if (!p_chd->check_is_cd() || !p_chd->check_is_gd())
+		{
+			p_cd = std::make_unique<cdrom_file>(p_chd.get());
+			return 1;
+		}
+		return 2;
+	}
+	catch (...)
+	{
+		p_cd.reset();
+		return p_chd && p_chd->opened() ? 2 : -1;
+	}
+}
+
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE int wasm_probe_tracks()
+{
+	return p_cd ? p_cd->get_last_track() : 0;
+}
+
+// out[0]=type, out[1]=frames, out[2]=pregap, out[3]=datasize, out[4]=gdrom flag
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE int wasm_probe_track_info(int track, uint32_t *out)
+{
+	if (!p_cd || track < 0 || track >= p_cd->get_last_track())
+		return -1;
+	const cdrom_file::track_info &t = p_cd->get_toc().tracks[track];
+	out[0] = t.trktype;
+	out[1] = t.frames;
+	out[2] = t.pregap;
+	out[3] = t.datasize;
+	out[4] = p_cd->is_gdrom() ? 1 : 0;
+	return 0;
+}
+
+// reads 2048 bytes of user data: sector lba of a CD track (counted from index 1),
+// or byte offset lba*2048 for DVD/raw CHDs (track ignored)
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE int wasm_probe_read(int track, uint32_t lba, uint8_t *out)
+{
+	try
+	{
+		if (p_cd)
+		{
+			if (track < 0 || track >= p_cd->get_last_track())
+				return -1;
+			if (p_cd->get_track_type(track) == cdrom_file::CD_TRACK_AUDIO)
+				return -1;
+			return p_cd->read_data(p_cd->get_track_start(track) + lba, out, cdrom_file::CD_TRACK_MODE1) ? 0 : -1;
+		}
+		if (!p_chd)
+			return -1;
+		uint64_t offset = uint64_t(lba) * 2048;
+		if (offset + 2048 > p_chd->logical_bytes())
+			return -1;
+		return p_chd->read_bytes(offset, out, 2048) ? -1 : 0;
+	}
+	catch (...)
+	{
+		return -1;
+	}
+}
+
+extern "C" EMSCRIPTEN_KEEPALIVE double wasm_probe_logical()
+{
+	return p_chd ? double(p_chd->logical_bytes()) : 0;
+}

+++ par_lib.js (new file, Emscripten JS library)
+addToLibrary({
+  wasm_par_enabled__deps: ['$Asyncify'],
+  wasm_par_enabled: function (hunkbytes, unitbytes, comp) {
+    Module['__asyncify'] = Asyncify;
+    if (!Module['parSetup']) return 0;
+    var p = comp >>> 2;
+    var list = [HEAPU32[p], HEAPU32[p + 1], HEAPU32[p + 2], HEAPU32[p + 3]];
+    return Module['parSetup'](hunkbytes >>> 0, unitbytes >>> 0, list) ? 1 : 0;
+  },
+  wasm_par_submit: function (item, data, length) {
+    Module['parSubmit'](item >>> 0, data >>> 0, length >>> 0);
+  },
+  wasm_par_yield__async: true,
+  wasm_par_yield: function () {
+    if (!Module['parActive']) return;
+    return Asyncify.handleSleep(function (wakeUp) { Module['parYield'](wakeUp); });
+  },
+});

    
  
    

    

  
    

    

    


    
  
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
  
    

    


  
    Settings
    
  
    
    
    
    
    
    
    Current: none. Files with the same name are replaced.
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    Screen info
      
    If the layout looks wrong on your device, a screenshot of this helps pin it down.
